reason: Names the mailbox of a new profile, which discovery turns into a server; no vocabulary role names a mail address yet. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.
Names the IMAP server of a mailbox that discovery cannot find; no vocabulary role names a mail server setting yet. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.
Names the login when it is not the full address, which some servers want; no vocabulary role names a mail server setting yet. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.
Chooses tls or starttls for the IMAP connection; no vocabulary role names a mail server setting yet. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.
Lists the server's short fixed set of folders, which has nothing to filter; the query arrives with `messages list`. Review when messages list ships.

Lists the few profiles on this computer, every one at once by design (WC-ACCT-12), as gcal's session list does; a filter would let a caller narrow it to one and read that as the only profile. Review if a computer commonly holds more profiles than fit one screen.

Sets an IMAP flag or keyword on an email (read, flagged, $Junk); no vocabulary role names a mail flag yet, and --add means a chat and --set an id across the family. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.
Takes an IMAP flag or keyword off an email; no vocabulary role names a mail flag yet, and --remove means a chat across the family. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.

Chooses the envelope mail the owner's rules let go, memo's mail delete moved here; no vocabulary role names a selection by rules yet, and --by groups a list across the family. Review when cli-base's vocabulary names one.

The vocabulary's --to is <chat>, where a messenger sends; a mail recipient is an address, and one --to for both is what every mail tool and the plan (§2.1) use. Review when cli-base decides whether --to names a chat or any recipient.
The vocabulary's --subject is <ref>, memo's topic reference; an email's Subject is free text and every mail tool calls it --subject. Review when cli-base gives mail's subject a word.
cli-base's vocabulary has no mail words yet; a cli-base PR adds them, and mail can take them only when cli-core moves past cli-base 0.68. Review when cli-core depends on a cli-base that has them.
